direction.help: Direction of the alternative hypothesis: 'two-sided', 'greater' or 'less'.

targetValue.help: The entered target value: μ₀ or σ²₀ for one sample, the hypothesised mean difference μ_d₀ for the paired test.

targetType.help: Whether the spread target value counts as a variance or as a standard deviation.

colRef1.help: Column reference of the first sample.

colRef2.help: Column reference of the second sample.

colRefsK.help: The column references of the k-sample test.

equalVariances.help: Whether equal variances are assumed: the pooled t-test instead of Welch with two samples, Fisher's ANOVA instead of Welch with k.

result.help: The result of the analysis as numbers: route, normality findings, main test (statistic, degrees of freedom, p, interval, decision), power, pairwise comparisons and residuals; `{ status: 'insufficient', reason }` while the inputs are not sufficient.

setCategory.help: Chooses what is being tested: the spread (Variances) or the location (Means). The result is recomputed from the new settings.

params.category: 'variance' or 'mean'. Any other value is an error.
params.command: The command as one object with category.

setTestType.help: Chooses the sample layout: one sample against a target value, two samples against each other, or k groups. The result is recomputed from the new settings.

params.testType: 'one', 'two', 'paired' or 'k'. Any other value is an error.
params.command: The command as one object with testType.

Analysis.status: Outcome of the analysis: “ok” when it was computed, “insufficient” while inputs are missing.
Analysis.reason: Only for “insufficient”: why nothing was computed (columns missing, fewer than 3 values, target missing, pairing, no variation, not computable).
Analysis.count: Only for “insufficient” with paired data: number of usable pairs.
Analysis.isK: True with more than two samples (ANOVA branch).
Analysis.allNormal: True when every sample passes the normality test (Anderson-Darling against α).
Analysis.alpha: Significance level α used for the computation.
Analysis.target: Resolved target value (variance tests), otherwise empty.
Analysis.samples: Statistics per sample; when paired, one sample holding the differences.
Analysis.route: The chosen main procedure, as the route under “Algorithm Routing” shows it. Normality is decided by the Anderson-Darling test alone, with p ≥ α. For variances: one sample always uses the χ² variance test, two samples the F-test when all are normal, otherwise Levene (Brown-Forsythe), k samples Bartlett or Levene. For means: when all samples are normal, the parametric test; otherwise it stays when every sample has n ≥ 20 (the rank test is added as a cross-check); otherwise the rank route. Parametric means the one-sample t-test, the Welch t-test (pooled t-test only when equal variances are assumed) or one-way ANOVA; the rank route means Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann-Whitney U or Kruskal-Wallis.
Analysis.varEquality: Test for equal variances with its verdict and the route step label; empty when not needed.
Analysis.main: Result of the main procedure: statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, interval and decision.
Analysis.anova: Only for k samples: ANOVA table, model fit and group statistics.
Analysis.numeric: Numeric output of the test: statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, interval, decision, power and notes.
Analysis.secondary: Cross-check with the rank test when the parametric procedure stays although samples are not normal; otherwise empty.
Analysis.power: Power, effect and required sample size; empty when not computed.
Analysis.pairwise: Pairwise comparisons after the overall test (k samples only) with procedure, comparisons and grouping letters.
Analysis.residualPlot: Residuals and fitted values for the residual plots; empty when there are none.
Analysis.notes: Notes on the interval as codes with the numbers filled in.
Analysis.pairInfo: Paired only: number of pairs and of dropped rows.

Numeric.df: Degrees of freedom; for the F-test and ANOVA the numerator degrees of freedom.
Numeric.df2: Denominator degrees of freedom; empty when there is only one.
Numeric.ci: Confidence interval [lower, upper]; empty without an interval.
Numeric.power: Power as a proportion; not for k samples.
Numeric.powerApprox: True when the power is a normal approximation (Bonett).
Numeric.notes: Notes on the interval as codes with numbers.

SampleStats.name: Column name of the sample.
SampleStats.sw: Shapiro-Wilk test: statistic W and p-value.
SampleStats.ad: Anderson-Darling test: statistic A² and p-value.
SampleStats.ciMean: Confidence interval of the mean; empty when not computable.
SampleStats.ciVariance: Confidence interval of the variance; empty when not computable.

Warning.code: Identifier of the note, equal to the text key.

NormRow.name: The normality test of this row, “Shapiro-Wilk” or “Anderson-Darling”. Column “Test”.
NormRow.stat: The test statistic with four decimals: W for Shapiro-Wilk, A² for Anderson-Darling. Column “Statistic”.
NormRow.p: The p-value of the test with four decimals. Column “p”.
NormRow.decisionText: The decision of the test: “Reject” when p < α, meaning the normality assumption is rejected, otherwise “Do not reject”. Column “Decision”.

AnovaRow.src: Source of variation: “Between Groups”, “Within Groups” or “Total”. Column “Source”.
AnovaRow.ss: Sum of squares: between groups Σ nᵢ(x̄ᵢ − x̄)², within groups the sum of squared deviations from the group mean, total the sum of both. Column “SS”.
AnovaRow.df: Degrees of freedom: k − 1 between groups, N − k within, N − 1 total. Column “df”.
AnovaRow.ms: Mean square: SS divided by df; “—” in the row Total. Column “MS”.
AnovaRow.f: F value: MS between divided by MS within, only in the row Between Groups, otherwise “—”. Column “F”.
AnovaRow.p: p-value of the F-test, only in the row Between Groups, otherwise “—”; below α the means differ significantly. Column “p”.

GroupRow.name: Name of the group, the column name from the data collection. Column “Group”.
GroupRow.n: Number of values in the group. Column “n”.
GroupRow.mean: Mean x̄ of the group with four decimals. Column “x̄”.
GroupRow.variance: Sample variance s² of the group with four decimals. Column “s²”.
GroupRow.ci: Confidence interval of the group mean with lower and upper bound, level 1 − α; only on the Fisher and Welch routes, otherwise the column is absent.
GroupRow.letters: The grouping letters (Compact Letter Display) from the pairwise comparisons: groups sharing a letter do not differ significantly, groups without a shared letter differ.

PairwiseCell.text: The Bonferroni-corrected p-value of the pair: p · m, at most 1, with m = k(k − 1)/2 pairs. From α upwards the pair counts as not significantly different, below as significant. “—” in empty cells.

PowerInfo.requiredLine: The line “Required n”, “per group” for two samples (equally sized groups): the smallest n between 4 and 5000 at which the power reaches the goal. If the goal is not reached by 5000, it reads “> 5000”. After it “Achieved” or “Not achieved” for the current power.

Result.route: The chosen main procedure, as the route under “Algorithm Routing” shows it. Normality is decided by the Anderson-Darling test alone, with p ≥ α. For variances: one sample always uses the χ² variance test, two samples the F-test when all are normal, otherwise Levene (Brown-Forsythe), k samples Bartlett or Levene. For means: when all samples are normal, the parametric test; otherwise it stays when every sample has n ≥ 20 (the rank test is added as a cross-check); otherwise the rank route. Parametric means the one-sample t-test, the Welch t-test (pooled t-test only when equal variances are assumed) or one-way ANOVA; the rank route means Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann-Whitney U or Kruskal-Wallis.
